notes: Aggregate only; located per-case evidence lives in the answer-key repo per the publishing rule. QUALIFICATIONS, each material: (1) the bug report for this run carried the vulnerability and reproduction prose fields, which were removed afterwards - no run made after commit 28695a4 is comparable. (2) 3 of the 5 NO_FIX are one unit whose fix was demonstrably correct - exploit probe blocked and workflow test green on all 5 rounds - and was reverted because its regression net contained tests that require attack-dependent behaviour; policy.on_exhausted has since changed to keep_best. (3) WPR is measured over the vetted 865-block net; an independent full-suite capture against the pristine base found 8 blocks lost in a unit test that pins a pre-fix value, outside that net, so WPR 1.0 means 'no damage within the vetted net', not 'no damage'. (4) node_modules is unpinned - the target app sets package-lock=false - so cross-run comparison is unsound. (5) the run's blind audit flagged contaminated on a single DENIED network egress attempt; out_of_tree and answer_key_pattern were both 0 and nothing was fetched, so blindness held; the classifier treats denied attempts as contaminating and has not been corrected.

located_detail_at: not yet scored; located detail is in the archived run store only, pending a sighted scoring pass in the answer-key repo
notes: 10 bugs, one OWASP class, three files. In-sandbox: 8 fixed, 1 already_remediated, 1 abandoned; basis 9 attested, 1 measured. $49.37 over 19 invocations, 151.6 minutes. Characterisation reuse was deliberately off so already_remediated was reachable at all -- with reuse on, later bugs in a file inherit the first one's oracle and the disposition cannot fire. NOT COMPARABLE with the earlier subset run: the bug report contract narrowed between them, the subsets and their oracle sets differ, and that engine's dispositions were measured where these are attested. A baseline was captured AFTER the run against the unpatched tree, in a single pass rather than the three the readiness doc requires, so flakiness is NOT excluded: unpatched showed zero failures in one suite and eight in the other, all dependent on outbound network this environment blocks. Against it the patched tree shows two new failures in the first suite and twelve in the second, and at least one of the two is a feature the application is supposed to provide -- so the workflow axis is not intact despite every task attesting that it was. No committed lockfile exists for the target, so the dependency set is whatever resolved that day and cross-run comparison is uncontrolled. The blind audit flagged the run contaminated; every flagged event was a DENIED attempt the sandbox refused, and the reasoning already applied once to reclassify a denied egress has not been applied to the two classifier entries that fired here.
